findings.title: Item resume bypasses the worktree registration guard
findings.description: Unlike `enter_slice_branch`, `_git_precondition` never calls `_require_registered_worktree`. In an unregistered linked worktree, CF can supply the primary checkout’s target, and `restore_target` can commit leftovers and switch branches before any later guard runs. Validate registration before mutating Git state; test that refusal leaves branches and files unchanged.

findings.title: Unresolved slice designs cannot resume after creation
findings.description: `slices-plan` uses `cf.undesigned_slices`, which stops selecting a slice once its design exists. Consequently, a successfully created design whose review exhausted its rounds cannot be retried or accepted: re-selection omits it, and reconciliation only permits completed, merged slices. The planning-batch test masks this by continually reporting no design for plan-scoped queries. Add coverage using the actual post-design lifecycle and allow unresolved artifacts to resume.

findings.title: Malformed report items escape schema-error handling
findings.description: `cast` does not validate the loaded JSON. A report with otherwise valid metadata and `"items": [null]` reaches `BatchItemRecord.from_json(None)`, raising `AttributeError`, which is not converted into `BatchReportLoadError`. Validate the complete report with a Pydantic schema and test malformed item shapes so item resume returns REJECTED rather than crashing.

findings.title: Resume preparation blocks the event loop
findings.description: The async path directly performs state/report file I/O, synchronous Git commands, and CF subprocess calls. Git commands can take 30 seconds; CF calls have no timeout. This violates the explicit sub-millisecond synchronous-work rule and prevents timely cancellation or concurrent async work. Offload blocking preparation and report writes, bound subprocess execution, and add a responsiveness test.

findings.title: Expected preparation failures violate the exit-code contract
findings.description: CF failures during source selection or dependency checks raise `ContextForgeError`/`ContextForgeNotAvailable`, neither of which this boundary handles. A missing pipeline instead reaches the broad `OSError` handler and is misleadingly reported as a batch-report write failure. Handle these failures at their actual boundaries, log the cause, and return the appropriate REJECTED or HALTED outcome with regression tests.
